name: Whistler Blackcomb
blurb: North America's largest lift-served area, two full mountains linked by the Peak 2 Peak gondola above a car-free village. Coastal storms bring heavy, frequent snow; low-elevation runs can turn wet in mild spells, so plan for the alpine.

name: Banff Sunshine
blurb: High-alpine bowls straddling the Continental Divide inside Banff National Park, with a long, cold season and reliably dry snow. A gondola climbs from the parking lot to the mid-mountain village and the only ski-in lodge in the park.

name: Lake Louise
blurb: Four mountain faces with big back bowls and some of the most photographed views in skiing. Cold Rockies temperatures keep the snow light but make layering and face protection essential mid-winter.

name: Revelstoke Mountain Resort
blurb: The biggest lift-served vertical in North America, deep Selkirk snowpack and an uncrowded, expert-leaning layout. The town is a hub for cat-skiing and heli-skiing operators.

name: Mont-Tremblant
blurb: Eastern Canada's flagship resort, with a pedestrian village, four mountain faces and a strong francophone après culture. Expect cold, firm conditions in January and better snow in February and March.

name: Big White
blurb: A ski-in/ski-out village with dry Okanagan snow, night skiing and one of the friendliest family layouts in Canada. Frequent valley cloud ('Big White-out') makes goggles with low-light lenses a must.

name: Vail
blurb: Seven legendary Back Bowls, endless groomers and a Tyrolean-style village. Weekend I-70 traffic from Denver is the main trade-off; fly into Eagle to skip it.

name: Aspen Snowmass
blurb: Four mountains on one ticket, from Buttermilk's gentle slopes to Highlands Bowl's hike-to steeps. The town delivers some of the best dining and après in the sport at a premium price.

name: Breckenridge
blurb: A historic mining town paired with five peaks and some of the highest lift-served terrain in North America. Altitude is real here, so hydrate and take day one easy.

name: Telluride
blurb: A box-canyon town linked by free gondola to Mountain Village, with famously short lift lines and dramatic San Juan views. Getting there takes effort, which is exactly why the slopes stay quiet.

name: Steamboat
blurb: Known for gladed tree skiing and light 'Champagne Powder', plus a genuine ranching town at the base. The Mahogany Ridge expansion added significant advanced terrain.

name: Park City Mountain
blurb: The largest single ski area in the United States, a short drive from Salt Lake City's airport, with a lively Main Street at the base. Variety is huge; the best snow is usually up high on the Canyons side.

name: Snowbird
blurb: Steep, deep Little Cottonwood Canyon terrain served by a 125-passenger tram, with seasons that often run into May. Canyon road closures for avalanche control can delay mornings after big storms.

name: Alta
blurb: A skiers-only mountain with a cult following for its snowfall and traverses into untracked lines. It connects to Snowbird with a combined ticket.

name: Deer Valley
blurb: A skiers-only resort celebrated for immaculate grooming, limited ticket sales and white-glove service. A major expansion is enlarging the terrain and adding a new base village.

name: Jackson Hole
blurb: Some of the most challenging lift-served terrain in North America, including Corbet's Couloir, plus an iconic aerial tram. Intermediates will find good groomers, but this mountain rewards strong skiers.

name: Big Sky
blurb: Huge terrain with very low skier density and a new generation of high-speed, heated-bubble lifts. Lone Peak's tram accesses serious expert lines above 3,300 m.

name: Palisades Tahoe
blurb: Two linked valleys famous for steep chutes and sunny spring skiing above Lake Tahoe. Sierra storms can be massive and wet; check chain controls on I-80 before driving.

name: Mammoth Mountain
airport: MMH Mammoth Yosemite / LAX (~5 h drive)
blurb: A volcanic peak with one of the longest seasons in North America, often skiing into June. Its terrain parks are among the best in the world.

name: Heavenly
blurb: Runs straddle the California–Nevada line with constant Lake Tahoe views, and South Lake Tahoe's casinos supply the nightlife. Great intermediate cruising; snowmaking is extensive.

name: Sun Valley
blurb: America's first destination ski resort, with consistent fall-line pitch on Bald Mountain and a refined, uncrowded feel. Snowfall is moderate, backed by strong snowmaking.

name: Stowe
blurb: Vermont's classic resort beneath Mount Mansfield, with the 'Front Four' steeps and a picture-book New England village. Conditions swing with Atlantic weather; midweek powder days are gold.

name: Killington
blurb: The 'Beast of the East', with six peaks, huge snowmaking and one of the longest seasons in the eastern US. Après along the Access Road is legendary.

name: Taos Ski Valley
blurb: Steep, sunny southern Rockies terrain with hike-to ridgeline chutes and a strong ski-school tradition. Pair it with Taos's art scene and New Mexican food.

name: Chamonix Mont-Blanc
blurb: The capital of extreme skiing beneath Mont Blanc, with separate ski areas along the valley and the off-piste Vallée Blanche from the Aiguille du Midi. Hire a guide for anything off the marked runs.

name: Val Thorens (Les 3 Vallées)
blurb: Europe's highest resort village and the snow-sure top of the vast 3 Vallées network. Treeless and exposed, it's superb in sun and challenging in storms.

name: Tignes – Val d'Isère
blurb: A high, glacier-backed linked area with a long season, World Cup pistes and some of the best lift-served off-piste in the Alps. Val d'Isère's après is famous.

name: Zermatt (Matterhorn)
airport: GVA Geneva / ZRH Zurich (~3.5 h by train)
blurb: A car-free village beneath the Matterhorn with glacier skiing all year and the option to ski across the border to Cervinia, Italy. Mountain restaurants are a highlight.

name: Verbier (4 Vallées)
blurb: A freeride mecca with legendary off-piste, home of the Freeride World Tour finals, and a glamorous après scene. The wider 4 Vallées adds plenty of cruising.

name: St. Anton am Arlberg
blurb: Birthplace of modern ski instruction and Austria's après-ski capital, linked with Lech and Zürs in the Ski Arlberg area. Steep, challenging pistes and deep off-piste.

name: Kitzbühel
blurb: A medieval town and home of the Hahnenkamm downhill, with broad cruising and excellent mountain huts. Lower altitude makes snowmaking important early season.

name: Ischgl (Silvretta Arena)
blurb: High, snow-sure terrain that links to duty-free Samnaun in Switzerland, plus big-name season-opening concerts and lively après.

name: Sölden
blurb: Two glaciers and three 3,000 m peaks give a long season; the World Cup opens here each October. Busy nightlife and big-mountain views.

name: Cortina d'Ampezzo
blurb: The 'Queen of the Dolomites' and a 2026 Winter Olympics venue, combining dramatic rock towers, sunny pistes and Italian style. Part of the huge Dolomiti Superski pass.

name: Val Gardena (Sella Ronda)
blurb: Gateway to the Sella Ronda circuit around the Sella massif, with superb value, grooming and mountain huts. Ideal for confident intermediates.

name: Grandvalira
blurb: The Pyrenees' largest area, with low prices, strong ski schools and duty-free shopping. Sunny, wide slopes suit beginners and families.

name: Åre
blurb: Scandinavia's biggest resort, with a lively village, World Cup history and long spring days. Mid-winter daylight is short and cold.

name: Niseko United
blurb: Siberian air over the Sea of Japan delivers some of the lightest, most consistent powder on earth. Four linked resorts, night skiing and Japanese onsen culture.

name: Hakuba Valley
blurb: Ten resorts in a 1998 Olympic valley with the steepest, most alpine terrain in Japan and easy access from Tokyo. Deep snow and great backcountry with a guide.

name: Gulmarg
blurb: A Himalayan freeride destination where one of the world's highest gondolas reaches Apharwat ridge. Huge off-piste at a fraction of Alpine prices; go with local guides and check travel advisories.

name: Thredbo
blurb: Australia's longest runs and biggest vertical, with an alpine village feel. Skiing runs roughly June to early October.

name: Perisher
blurb: The Southern Hemisphere's largest ski area across four interlinked areas. Wind and snow cover vary a lot; mid-season (July–August) is most reliable.

name: Coronet Peak & The Remarkables
blurb: Two ski areas minutes from Queenstown, the adventure capital of the world. Coronet Peak adds night skiing; The Remarkables has great park and alpine terrain.

name: Valle Nevado
blurb: High Andes skiing within reach of Santiago, linked with neighbouring areas into one of South America's biggest domains. Clear, dry winters and serious altitude.

name: Portillo
blurb: A historic, single-hotel resort on a high Andean lake with steep terrain and a famously sociable week-long stay format.
